questions.question: True or False: When n Scrum teams are working on a product, there should always be only 1 Product Owner but 1-n Scrum Masters.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: One Product Owner per product; a Scrum Master can serve one or several teams.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: One Product Owner per product, while a Scrum Master may serve multiple teams.

questions.question:
What is the main accountability of a Project Manager in Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Supporting the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: Supporting the Product Owner is a service of the Scrum Master; Scrum has no Project Manager role.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tracking the progress of a Release.
choices.explanation: Tracking progress is done by the Scrum Team itself; Scrum has no Project Manager role.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There are no Project Managers in Scrum.
choices.explanation: Scrum defines only three accountabilities: Product Owner, Scrum Master and Developers. There is no Project Manager.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Managing Risks.
choices.explanation: Risks are managed by the Scrum Team through short Sprints and empiricism; Scrum has no Project Manager role.

questions.question:
What does a burn-down chart measure in a project?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Work remaining across time.
choices.explanation: A burn-down chart shows work remaining over time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Business value delivered by the team.
choices.explanation: It does not measure business value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Budget remaining across time.
choices.explanation: It does not measure budget.

questions.question:
Which statement explains when a Product Backlog Item is considered "Done"?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the Product Owner declares it to be "Done".
choices.explanation: Done is defined by the Definition of Done, not by the Product Owner's declaration.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the Developers agrees that it is "Done".
choices.explanation: Done is not decided by agreement; it depends on the Definition of Done.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When it is potentially releasable.
choices.explanation: An item is Done when it meets the Definition of Done and is usable, potentially releasable.

questions.question:
Which statements about the Product Backlog are correct?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Product Backlog contains only items that are completely refined.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog is not fully refined; items lower down are less detailed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the Product Backlog, Items at the top are usually smaller than on the bottom.
choices.explanation: Higher-ordered items are usually clearer and more detailed, therefore smaller.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Backlog is never baselined.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog is never fixed; it evolves continuously.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct about "technical debt"?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: If you have a high level of "technical debt", it could lead to false assumptions about the current state of the system.
choices.explanation: Technical debt can create a false impression of the system's true state.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If you have "technical debt", no further features should be developed until the "technical debt" is fixed.
choices.explanation: Development does not have to stop; technical debt is managed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It creates uncertainty, because when you add more and more features more and more problems will occur.
choices.explanation: Technical debt increases uncertainty as functionality grows.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the task of the Product Owner to take it into account during the release planning.
choices.explanation: Release planning is not a Scrum concept and technical debt concerns the whole Scrum Team.

questions.question:
The Developers have trouble understanding a Sprint Backlog item – what should they do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask the Scrum Master to explain it to them.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner, not the Scrum Master, clarifies Product Backlog items.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Don't touch the item until the Sprint Review to discuss it with the Product Owner again.
choices.explanation: Waiting until the Sprint Review delays the work and risks the Sprint Goal.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Collaborate with the Product Owner immediately to receive a better understanding.
choices.explanation: Developers collaborate with the Product Owner as soon as questions arise to clarify the work.

questions.question:
What kind of testing should be done during the Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Test Driven Development.
choices.explanation: Test Driven Development is one practice, but Scrum does not prescribe it, and it is not the only testing needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acceptance Tests.
choices.explanation: Acceptance tests are only part of the testing needed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Unit Tests.
choices.explanation: Unit tests alone are not enough to ensure a usable Increment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All kind of test required to create a working Increment.
choices.explanation: All testing needed to meet the Definition of Done and produce a usable Increment is done within the Sprint.

questions.question:
Which Scrum accountability is responsible to do all the work required to turn Product Backlog in potentially releasable items?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Business Analyst.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Business Analyst role.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Project Manager.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Project Manager role.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers are the people in the Scrum Team committed to creating any aspect of a usable Increment each Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Stakeholders do not do the work of the Scrum Team.

questions.question: True or False: The Product Owner has to maximize the value – more features always bring more value. Therefore, the Product Owner has to maximize the number of features in a Sprint.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: More features do not mean more value; outcomes matter, not output.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Value comes from outcomes, not from the number of features; unused features add cost without value.

questions.question:
Which two of the following services are expected from a Scrum Master to a Product Owner?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Master should help the Product Owner to find techniques for managing the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master helps find techniques for effective Product Goal definition and Product Backlog management.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Master should help the Product Owner to do the documentation.
choices.explanation: Documentation is not a specific Scrum Master service to the Product Owner.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Master should remove impediments for the Scrum Team (incl. Product Owner).
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master causes the removal of impediments for the whole Scrum Team, including the Product Owner.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master should act as a "middleman" between the Product Owner and the Developers.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master should foster direct collaboration, not act as a go-between.

questions.question: True or False: Only the Developers are influencing the Definition of Done, no one else.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done is created by the Scrum Team, or by the organization's standards; not by the Developers alone.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The organization's standards and the whole Scrum Team influence the Definition of Done, not only the Developers.

questions.question:
When can a Sprint be cancelled?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.
choices.explanation: A Sprint can be cancelled by the Product Owner when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the Developers are asking the Product Owner to do it.
choices.explanation: The Developers' request alone is not a reason; only an obsolete Sprint Goal justifies cancellation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the Business Analyst is asking the Product Owner to do it.
choices.explanation: There is no Business Analyst role in Scrum, and requests are not a valid reason.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete and no items are "Done" yet.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Goal becoming obsolete is enough; whether items are Done does not matter.

questions.question:
If the Product Owner has concerns about the Definition of Done (DoD) – what should the Product Owner do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Product Owner should discuss the Definition of Done with the Developers.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done belongs to the Scrum Team; concerns are discussed together, for example at the Sprint Retrospective.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner should change the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner cannot change the Definition of Done alone.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner should ask the Scrum Master to change the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not change the Definition of Done.

questions.question:
Which of the following are not required by Scrum?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Using User Stories.
choices.explanation: User Stories are a complementary practice, not required by Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have a Product Owner.
choices.explanation: A Product Owner is required by Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Answering the "three questions" in the Daily Scrums.
choices.explanation: The three questions were removed from the Scrum Guide; they are not required.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Having time boxed Scrum Events.
choices.explanation: Scrum events are timeboxed; this is required.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Have a Sprint Backlog.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog is a required Scrum artifact.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Using the concept of Story Points.
choices.explanation: Story Points are an optional estimation technique, not required by Scrum.

questions.question:
Which two of the following answers are not correct about the Product Owner accountability?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Product Owner decides which developer does what.
choices.explanation: Developers self-manage who does what; the Product Owner does not assign work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner has to participate in the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is not required at the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner measures the progress of a release.
choices.explanation: Monitoring progress toward goals is something the Product Owner can do, so this statement is not incorrect.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner is responsible for maximizing the value.
choices.explanation: Maximizing the value of the product is the core accountability of the Product Owner.

questions.question: True or False: Scrum can only be used to develop products, not to maintain/sustain existing ones.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Scrum is used for developing and sustaining products.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Scrum applies to both developing and sustaining complex products.

questions.question:
What can be done to reduce technical debt?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Improve the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: A stronger Definition of Done reduces the creation of technical debt.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Include external QA.
choices.explanation: External QA adds handovers and does not prevent debt; quality is the Developers' responsibility.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have hardening Sprints.
choices.explanation: Hardening Sprints do not exist in Scrum; they hide undone work.

questions.question: True or False: The Scrum Master can decide which Scrum Events are required in the Scrum project.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Scrum events are mandatory; the Scrum Master cannot remove them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: All Scrum events are required; omitting one removes an inspection and adaptation opportunity.

questions.question:
Which of the following is not a feedback loop in Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Sprint Review.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review is an inspection and adaptation loop with stakeholders.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Sprint Planning.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning uses feedback to plan the next Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Backlog Grooming.
choices.explanation: Grooming, now refinement, is an ongoing activity, not a Scrum event or formal feedback loop.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is the daily inspection and adaptation loop.

questions.question: True or False: When n Scrum teams are working on a product, there are n Sprint Backlogs but only 1 Product Backlog.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Each Scrum Team has its own Sprint Backlog, while one product has a single Product Backlog.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: One product has one Product Backlog; each team creates its own Sprint Backlog.

questions.question:
Which statement describes best how the Product Backlog is impacted by changes in the product environment?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Product Backlog should always follow the Product Owners plan and should not reflect the changes at all.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog must reflect changes; it is not a fixed plan.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Backlog should be very high level and therefore tolerate such changes.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog has different levels of detail, but it adapts to changes rather than staying vague.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Backlog should evolve and reflect the environment changes.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog is emergent and adapts to changes in the environment.

questions.question:
Which of the following are not allowed in Scrum?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Using User Stories.
choices.explanation: User Stories are allowed as a complementary practice.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Having two Product Owners in a Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: A Scrum Team has exactly one Product Owner.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A Sprint 0.
choices.explanation: There is no Sprint 0; every Sprint produces a usable Increment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A Release Sprint.
choices.explanation: There are no release Sprints; every Sprint produces a usable Increment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Using Story Points.
choices.explanation: Story Points are allowed as a complementary practice.

questions.question: True or False: When two Scrum Teams are working on the same product you should normalize their estimations to be able to compare their performance.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Estimates are specific to each team; normalizing them to compare performance leads to gaming metrics.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Comparing teams via normalized estimates is not meaningful and is harmful; value delivered matters.

questions.question: True or False: The Product Owner can nominate a "Lead Developer" as a single point of contact.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: There are no lead roles among Developers; the Product Owner works with all of them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Lead Developer; all Developers collaborate directly with the Product Owner.

questions.question:
Which of the following answers is correct about the Product Owner accountability?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Product Owner is not part of the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is a member of the Scrum Team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner creates all items in the Product Backlog on his own.
choices.explanation: Anyone can contribute Product Backlog items; the Product Owner does not create them all alone.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner is responsible to explain Product Backlog Items and to answer questions.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner ensures Product Backlog items are understood and answers questions.

questions.question:
Which statement is correct about the Sprint Backlog?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: It doesn't need to have detail.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog needs enough detail for the Developers to inspect progress at the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It has just enough detail.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog has enough detail for the Developers to make progress and change as they learn.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It has all the details.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog emerges; it does not need all details upfront.

questions.question: True or False: Two Scrum Teams are working on the same product. Do they have to share the same Definition of Ready?

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Definition of Ready is not a Scrum concept; teams are free to use or not use one.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Definition of Ready is not part of Scrum, so there is no obligation to share one.

questions.question: True or False: It is not allowed that the Product Owner is a Developer (part of the "Developers") at the same time.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner can also do development work; they then participate as a Developer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Guide allows the Product Owner to also work on Sprint Backlog items as a Developer.

questions.question:
Which 2 of the following are an indication for an item to be ready for development?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The item is refined and small enough to fit in one Sprint.
choices.explanation: Items that can be Done within a Sprint are considered ready for selection.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All stakeholder have agreed to prioritize it.
choices.explanation: Stakeholder agreement is not needed; the Product Owner decides the order.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The item is estimated (e.g. in Story Points).
choices.explanation: Refinement adds details such as size; an estimate helps the Developers make a forecast.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The item is smaller than 15 Story Points.
choices.explanation: There is no size threshold in Scrum.

questions.question: True or False: To be self-management means, that it is okay for the Developers to not do the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is a mandatory event; self-management happens within the framework.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Self-management means deciding who does what, when and how, within Scrum; skipping events is not allowed.

questions.question:
Which of the following should a Scrum Master do to start a project?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask the Lead Developer to explain the IT architecture.
choices.explanation: Understanding architecture is useful but there is no Lead Developer role and it is not the first step for team building.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ask the Developers to introduce themselves to each other and tell about their skills and background.
choices.explanation: Helping people get to know each other's skills fosters collaboration and self-management.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ensure, that all team members have a first ticket assigned to them.
choices.explanation: Developers self-manage and select their own work.

questions.question: True or False: All items in the Product Backlog usually have the same size.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Items vary in size; higher-ordered items are usually smaller and more detailed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Product Backlog items vary in size and detail; they are not all the same size.

questions.question: True or False: Does a Product Backlog Item have an item "Owner".

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Product Backlog items are owned collectively; the Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not assign owners to individual items; the Product Owner is accountable for the whole Product Backlog.

questions.question: True or False: The Product Owner is not part of the Scrum Team.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team consists of one Scrum Master, one Product Owner and Developers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is part of the Scrum Team.

questions.question:
Which Scrum accountabilities have to attend the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not have to attend the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Project Manager.
choices.explanation: There is no Project Manager in Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is for the Developers; they are required to attend.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is not required, unless working on Sprint Backlog items as a Developer.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Business Analyst.
choices.explanation: There is no Business Analyst role in Scrum.

questions.question:
Which two of the following contribute the most to the Scrum Value "Focus"?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Having a Burn-Down-Chart.
choices.explanation: A burn-down chart is optional and is not the main focus driver.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Having a Sprint Goal.
choices.explanation: A Sprint Goal gives the team a clear focus.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Using Story Points.
choices.explanation: Story Points are an optional estimation technique and do not drive focus.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Having time boxed events.
choices.explanation: Timeboxes help the team focus on what matters most.

questions.question:
Which of the following best describes the Scrum Pillar "Transparency"?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The whole process should be visible to everyone.
choices.explanation: Not everything needs to be visible to everyone; transparency concerns those doing and receiving the work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The process should be visible to the key stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Transparency is not only for key stakeholders.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Significant aspects of the process must be visible to those responsible for the outcome.
choices.explanation: Significant aspects of the process and work must be visible to those responsible for the outcome.

questions.question: True or False: The Product Backlog is baselined before the Sprint 0.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: There is no Sprint 0 and the Product Backlog is never baselined.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog is never baselined; it evolves continuously, and there is no Sprint 0.

questions.question:
Which of the following are Scrum Values?
(choose all that apply)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Respect.
choices.explanation: Respect is a Scrum value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Focus.
choices.explanation: Focus is a Scrum value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inspection.
choices.explanation: Inspection is a pillar of empiricism, not a value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Collaboration.
choices.explanation: Collaboration is important, but it is not one of the five Scrum values.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Commitment.
choices.explanation: Commitment is a Scrum value.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Maximize Value.
choices.explanation: Maximizing value is the Product Owner's accountability, not a Scrum value.

choices.label: G
choices.text: Courage.
choices.explanation: Courage is a Scrum value.

choices.label: H
choices.text: Openness.
choices.explanation: Openness is a Scrum value.

questions.question: True or False: Self-management means, that the team can decide which Scrum events are needed.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Self-management applies within the Scrum framework; events are not optional.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: All Scrum events are mandatory; self-management covers who does what, when and how.

questions.question: True or False: Following Scrum, there can be a maximum of one release per Sprint.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Multiple Increments can be created and released within a Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Scrum allows several releases within a Sprint; the Product Owner decides when to release.

questions.question:
Which of the following are mandatory in Scrum?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Do Sprint Planning events.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is a mandatory Scrum event.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Do Daily Scrums.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is a mandatory Scrum event.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Have a Product Owner.
choices.explanation: A Product Owner is a mandatory accountability in Scrum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use Story Points.
choices.explanation: Story Points are optional.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Use User Stories.
choices.explanation: User Stories are optional.

questions.question: True or False: The Scrum Master can decide which Scrum Artifacts are required in the Scrum project.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Scrum artifacts are mandatory; the Scrum Master cannot remove them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: All Scrum artifacts are required; Scrum's elements are immutable.

questions.question:
How is budgeting done in a Scrum Project?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ideally budgeting is done every Sprint.
choices.explanation: Each Sprint is an opportunity to inspect value and reconsider investment, so budgeting can be revisited every Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Scrum doesn't need the team to care about budget.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team does care about cost and value, and the Product Owner makes investment decisions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Budgeting is done based on the Product Backlog as a baseline.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog is not a baseline; it evolves.

questions.question:
The collaboration between the Developers and the Product Owner is very important for the product. Which of the following is the least productive way for the Scrum Master to improve this collaboration?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Master should act as a go-between for them.
choices.explanation: Acting as a go-between harms direct collaboration and is the least productive option.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Master should teach them techniques to improve it.
choices.explanation: Teaching collaboration techniques is a useful service from the Scrum Master.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Master should suggest new collaboration tools.
choices.explanation: Suggesting tools can help collaboration.

questions.question:
Which Scrum Event can be compared to the use of a "lessons learned meeting"?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Sprint Review.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review inspects the product, not lessons learned on the process.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum inspects progress toward the Sprint Goal.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Sprint Retrospective.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective is where the team reflects on how to improve, similar to lessons learned.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Sprint Planning.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning plans the upcoming Sprint.

questions.question: True or False: The Product Backlog should have just enough detail.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Items are refined to the level of detail needed; higher-ordered items have more detail.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Over-detailing items too early is waste, but having no detail at all prevents planning.

questions.question:
Developers are self-managing, which of the following do they manage?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Product Backlog ordering.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner orders the Product Backlog.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When to release, based on its progress.
choices.explanation: Release decisions belong to the Product Owner.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sprint Backlog.
choices.explanation: Developers own and manage the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stakeholders for the Sprint Review.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner invites stakeholders.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sprint length.
choices.explanation: Sprint length is decided by the Scrum Team, not the Developers alone, and it is usually stable.

questions.question:
Which of the following is required by Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sprint Retrospective.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective is a mandatory Scrum event.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Developers must stand up at the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: Standing up is a common practice, but not required by Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sprint Burndown Chart.
choices.explanation: Burn-down charts are optional.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Release Planning.
choices.explanation: Release planning is not part of Scrum.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All of the above.
choices.explanation: Since only the Sprint Retrospective is required, this answer is wrong.

questions.question:
A Scrum Master is working with a Scrum Team that has Developers in different physical locations. The Developers meet in a variety of meeting rooms and have much to do logistically (for example: reserve meeting rooms and set up conference calls) before the Daily Scrum. What action should the Scrum Master take?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set up the meeting and tell the Scrum Team that is how it will be done.
choices.explanation: Imposing a solution undermines self-management.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Allow the Developers to self-manage and determine for themselves what to do.
choices.explanation: Developers self-manage and can solve their own logistic problems.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inform management and ask them to solve it.
choices.explanation: Escalating to management for a team issue removes autonomy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ask the Developers to alternate who is responsible for meeting setup.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master should not impose a solution, even a rotation.

questions.question:
When multiple Scrum Teams are working on the same product, should all of their Increments be integrated every Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, but only for Scrum Teams whose work has dependencies.
choices.explanation: All teams working on the same product contribute to one integrated Increment, dependencies or not.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, in order to accurately inspect what is done.
choices.explanation: Integrating every Sprint gives full transparency on what is really done.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No, that's far too hard and must be done in a hardening Sprint.
choices.explanation: There are no hardening Sprints in Scrum; integration is part of Done.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No, each Scrum Team stands alone.
choices.explanation: Teams working on the same product contribute to a single integrated Increment.

questions.question:
Which two things should the Scrum Team do during the first Sprint?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Make up a plan for the rest of the project.
choices.explanation: Planning the rest of the project upfront is not empirical.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create at least one valuable, useful Increment.
choices.explanation: Every Sprint, including the first, should produce a valuable, useful Increment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Build at least one piece of valuable functionality.
choices.explanation: Delivering at least one piece of valuable functionality is the goal of every Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Define the major product features and a release plan architecture.
choices.explanation: Defining a release plan architecture upfront is not the goal of the first Sprint.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Analyze, describe, and document the requirements for the subsequent Sprints.
choices.explanation: Documenting requirements for later Sprints is not a Sprint goal.

questions.question:
What is the timebox for the Sprint Planning event?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whenever it is done.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning has a timebox.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Monthly.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is held at the start of each Sprint, not monthly.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 4 hours for a one-month Sprint.
choices.explanation: Four hours is the timebox for the Sprint Review for a one-month Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 8 hours for a one-month Sprint.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is timeboxed to a maximum of eight hours for a one-month Sprint.

questions.question:
Who owns the Sprint Backlog?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not own the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog belongs to the Developers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not own the Sprint Backlog.

questions.question:
What is the Product Owner responsible for during the Sprint Retrospective?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Participating as a Scrum Team member.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner participates as a full member of the Scrum Team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner should not take part in Sprint Retrospective.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is part of the Scrum Team and takes part in the Retrospective.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Capturing requirements for the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective is not about capturing requirements.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Summarizing and reporting the discussions to the stakeholders that they represent in the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective is internal to the Scrum Team; it is not a reporting meeting.

questions.question: True or False: The Definition of Ready shows the team when Product Backlog Items are ready to be selected for the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Ready does not exist in Scrum. Scrum only says that items which can be Done by the Scrum Team within one Sprint are deemed ready for selection in Sprint Planning.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Ready is not a Scrum concept. In Scrum, items that can be Done within one Sprint are considered ready for selection; this readiness comes from refinement, not from a Definition of Ready.

questions.question: True or False: When 3 products are developed using Scrum, there can be only a single Product Owner for all products.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Scrum requires one Product Owner per product, not one Product Owner for all products. Nothing forces the three products to share the same Product Owner.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Each product has its own Product Owner. One person may be the Product Owner of the three products, but Scrum does not require it: each product could also have a different Product Owner.

questions.question:
The Product Owner is not available and cannot answer the Developers' questions before Sprint Planning. Therefore, the Developers feel a high level of uncertainty to make a reliable forecast. What should the team do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Extend the duration of the current Sprint and try to answer all questions.
choices.explanation: Sprints are never extended; the next Sprint starts immediately after the previous one.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Sprint Planning meeting should be cancelled or postponed.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is a mandatory event that starts the Sprint; it is not postponed because of uncertainty.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The upcoming Sprint should be cancelled.
choices.explanation: Only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint, and only when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete; uncertainty is not a reason.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Developers should make the best decisions possible with the information available, and adapt as they learn more.
choices.explanation: Scrum is built for uncertainty: the Developers plan with what they know, start the Sprint and realign with the Product Owner as soon as they are available.
